editorial:
Imagine living in a gray, boring city where every day feels exactly the same. That is exactly how Paul feels in this story. He is a young guy working a dead-end job in Pittsburgh back in the early 1900s, and he absolutely hates his life. While everyone around him just accepts their lot, Paul spends all his time daydreaming about fancy clothes, art, and a life of luxury. He feels like he was born for something bigger, but he is stuck in a world that does not care about his dreams. It creates a really sad but relatable vibe for anyone who has ever felt out of place.

You will probably love how the movie shows the contrast between his dull home and the bright lights of New York City. The acting is solid, and it really makes you feel for Paul, even when he makes bad choices. The pacing is a bit slow at times since it is an older TV movie, but it keeps you interested. If you enjoy character studies, you should definitely check this out. Since it is a rare find, you might want to hunt for a digital rental on Apple TV or see if you can add the Blu-ray to your physical collection to keep the quality high.
endingExplained: After stealing money to fund his dream life in New York, Paul finally gets to experience the luxury he always wanted. However, the guilt and the fear of getting caught start to eat him alive. He realizes that he can never truly escape his past or his identity. In the final scenes, feeling trapped and hopeless, Paul decides to take his own life. He ends his journey because the real world could never match the perfect fantasy in his head.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about dreamers and tragic characters.
